parts.text: In this experiment, you will investigate a circuit containing different combinations of resistors. The circuit has been set up for you. Carry out the following instructions, referring to Fig. 2.1. Fig. 2.1

ms.label: 2(a)(i)
ms.text: V all < 4.00 (V) and to at least 1dp

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Calculate a resistance R 1 using your values from (a)(i) and the equation R 1 = V 1 I 1 . R 1 = .................................................... [1]

parts.label: i
parts.text: (b) (i) Connect both resistors in series between terminals P and Q as shown in Fig. 2.2. Fig. 2.2 Switch on. Measure the potential difference V 2 and the current I 2 in the circuit. V 2 = .......................................................... I 2 = .......................................................... [1] Switch off.

ms.label: 2(b)(i)
ms.text: I all < 2.00 (A) and to at least 2dp

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Calculate a resistance R 2 using your values from (b)(i) and the equation R 2 = V 2 (I 2 × 2) . R 2 = .................................................... [1]

parts.label: i
parts.text: (c) (i) Connect both resistors in parallel between terminals P and Q as shown in Fig. 2.3. Fig. 2.3 Switch on. Measure the potential difference V 3 and the current I 3 in the circuit. V 3 = .......................................................... I 3 = .......................................................... [1] Switch off.

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Calculate a resistance R 3 using your values from (c)(i) and the equation R 3 = (V 3 × 2) I 3 . R 3 = .................................................... [1]

ms.label: 2(c)(ii)
ms.text: R values all to consistent 2 or consistent 3 significant figures
